title: I do/work/like etc. (present simple)
subtitle: I work / he works
summary: Use the present simple for things that are true in general or happen all the time, and add -s after he, she and it.

lesson.heading: Things that are true in general
lesson.text: Two students stand in front of a big bookshelf with books in their hands. Books are part of their life, so we say: *They read a lot.* A man takes a bite of an ice-cream and smiles. Ice-cream is something he always enjoys, so we say: *He likes ice-cream.* This is the **present simple**.

lesson.heading: he works / she lives / it rains
lesson.text: After **he**, **she**, **it** and one person or thing, the verb ends in **-s**. Remember that **have** becomes **has**.

examples.text: I work in a shop. My brother **works** in a bank.
Lucy **lives** in London. Her parents **live** in Scotland.

lesson.heading: Spelling of the -s form
rows: pass -> passes, finish -> finishes, watch -> watches
study -> studies, try -> tries, fly -> flies

lesson.heading: When we use the present simple
lesson.text: We use it for things that are true in general, and for things that happen sometimes or all the time.

examples.text: Your English is good. You **speak** very well.
Tim **works** very hard. He **starts** at 7.30 and **finishes** at 8 o'clock in the evening.
It **costs** a lot of money to build a hospital.

lesson.heading: always / never / often / usually / sometimes
lesson.text: These words tell us how often something happens. They go **before** the verb.

examples.text: I **sometimes walk** to work, but not very often.

lesson.text: Never forget the -s after he, she and it: *my brother works in a bank*, not ~~my brother work~~.

exercises.prompt: I work in a shop. My brother ___ in a bank.
exercises.explanation: My brother = he, so the verb takes -s: works.

exercises.prompt: The shops in the city centre usually ___ at 9 o'clock in the morning.
exercises.explanation: The shops = they, so there is no -s.

exercises.prompt: The City Museum ___ at 5 o'clock in the evening.
exercises.explanation: The museum = it, so the verb takes -s: closes.

exercises.prompt: How do you write the he/she/it form of each verb?
Tina is a teacher. She ___ mathematics to young children.
exercises.explanation: Verbs that end in -ch take -es: teaches.

exercises.prompt: Peter's car is always dirty. He never ___ it.
exercises.explanation: Verbs that end in -sh take -es: washes. Never goes before the verb.
This is always true, so we use the present simple. Water = it, so: boils.

exercises.prompt: A woman sits down with a big bowl of fruit in front of her. Fruit is what she eats every day. ___ a lot of fruit.
exercises.explanation: She + eats. This is true in general, not only now.

exercises.prompt: A man holds a tennis racket and says: Tennis is my favourite sport. ___ tennis.
exercises.explanation: He + plays. It is something he does all the time.

exercises.prompt: Make a sentence with these words.
exercises.answer: I never go to the cinema.
exercises.explanation: never goes before the verb: I never go.

exercises.prompt: Make a sentence with these words.
exercises.explanation: Martina = she, so works. always goes before the verb.

exercises.statement: Sue gets always to work early.
exercises.explanation: Sue always gets to work early. always goes before the verb, not after it.
